examples.title: List sessions, windows, panes and clients
examples.description: Read current scalar listings from a private server. Each detached session has one window and pane; no clients are attached.
examples.output:
Session: demo ($0)
Session: worker ($1)
Windows: 2; panes: 2; clients: 0

examples.title: Look up live entities by identity
examples.description: Match successful lookups with Some and missing entities with None. The control connection supplies a client to find and is disposed before the owned server.
examples.output:
session: Some "demo"
window: Some "shell"
pane: Some true
client: Some true
missing: [false; false; false; false]

examples.title: Filter scalar listings and captured relations
examples.description: Compare native sequence filtering with portable F# filters. Capture the hierarchy before following pane and window relations; listing alone does not capture children.
examples.output:
native: ["demo"]
portable: ["demo"]
windows: ["shell"]
panes: 1
parents: ["demo"]
control clients: 1

examples.title: Read captured and uncaptured state
examples.description: Pattern match CaptureState before reading relations or active entities, and option before using nullable pane fields. Capturing returns a fresh handle; a captured empty relation is different from an uncaptured one.
examples.output:
Sessions have not been captured.
The captured active pane has a path and command.
The original handle is still uncaptured.
Captured sessions can be empty.

examples.title: Handle zero, one and multiple matches
examples.description: Select one session without using exceptions for ordinary cardinality outcomes. Match Ok, Error NoMatches and Error MultipleMatches explicitly.
examples.output:
One match: demo
No match: NoMatches
Two matches: MultipleMatches

examples.title: Keep absence, cancellation and failure distinct
examples.description: None means a successful read found no matching session. A cancelled operation, invalid client name and stopped server still raise exceptions; ownership scopes clean up independently of the caller token.
examples.output:
A successful lookup can return None.
Cancellation remains OperationCanceledException.
A blank client name remains ArgumentException.
A stopped server remains a LibTmuxException.

examples.title: Create an owned session, window and split pane
examples.description: Use core LibTmux ownership scopes for construction, then the F# Pane.split helper. F# has no separate session or window constructor; disposing the owned window also stops its split panes.
examples.output:
Created session demo and window editor.
Windows: 2; panes: 3

examples.title: Send literal input and capture completed output
examples.description: Type a shell command literally, press the named Enter key, and wait for its private completion signal before capturing output. Timeout and command failures escape the program after scoped cleanup; cancellation does not undo dispatched input.
examples.output: api capture ready

examples.title: Query every level and let tmux narrow the listing
examples.description: Read sessions, windows and panes through one query vocabulary. tmux drops rows a filter cannot keep, every returned row is rechecked, and a screen search finds the pane showing a line. atMostOne finds an object or reports it absent, and refuses several.
examples.output:
logged: true
named: Ok "build"
tailing: ["logs"]
make panes: 1
error row: Some 1
active panes: 2
deploy: absent true, then found true
at most one of every session: refused

examples.title: Send a command, wait for its output and run to an exit status
examples.description: Type a line and wait for what it prints, not for its echo. Wait for a condition over the whole screen, then run a command and read its exit status and output.
examples.output:
ready: true
counted: true
run: exit 4, output ["a"; "b"]
screen shows the run: true

examples.title: Follow live server state
examples.description: Keep a current copy of a server's sessions, windows and panes as tmux announces changes, and wait until it shows a state instead of polling.
examples.output:
windows: shell, logs
sleeping panes: 1
newer view: true

examples.title: Watch several panes through one control client
examples.description: Attach one control client, then follow two panes' output as each event names its pane. Each pane's end arrives as TmuxPaneGoneEvent in the order the panes were given.
examples.output:
build: ok
test: ok
ended in order given: true

examples.title: Describe a session, add a window with a chain, and bound every command
examples.description: Create a session from F# records in one call: the first window is the one tmux makes with the session, and each split goes beside the pane before it. Add a window with a command chain, then read through a handle whose commands each get five seconds.
examples.output:
editor: 1 panes
logs: 3 panes
watch: 2 panes

examples.title: Open and connect to an owned server
examples.description: Distinguish an endpoint handle from a discovered server. Connection discovery returns an immutable replacement without capturing child relations.
examples.output:
Open records an endpoint; Connect discovers the running server.
The original handle stays unmaterialized; relations remain uncaptured.

examples.title: List sessions, windows, panes and clients
examples.description: Read scalar listings from two detached sessions on a private server. Fresh rows do not imply captured child relations.
examples.output:
Session: demo ($0)
Session: worker ($1)
Windows: 2; panes: 2; clients: 0

examples.title: Create a session, window and split pane
examples.description: Create entities directly inside an owned server scope, then read the session and window children. The outer scope stops its daemon and all created entities.
examples.output:
Created session demo and window editor.
Windows: 2; panes: 3

examples.title: Filter listings and captured relations
examples.description: Compare LINQ with translated expression and document predicates, preserve cancellation, and capture the hierarchy before filtering its children.
examples.output:
Cancelled filtering remains OperationCanceledException.
LINQ, expression and document filters: demo; captured parent: demo

examples.title: Find entities and distinguish failures
examples.description: Use typed required lookups, nullable absence and explicit errors. Cancellation, invalid input and a stopped server remain exceptions.
examples.output:
A successful lookup can return null.
Required lookup reports TmuxObjectNotFoundException.
Cancellation remains OperationCanceledException.
A blank pane target remains ArgumentException.
A stopped server remains a LibTmuxException.

examples.title: Read captured and uncaptured state
examples.description: Capture a new immutable hierarchy, check optional pane state, and distinguish an empty captured relation from one that has not been read.
examples.output:
Sessions have not been captured.
The captured active pane has a path and command.
The original handle is still uncaptured.
Captured sessions can be empty.

examples.title: Send input and capture signalled output
examples.description: Send literal text and a named Enter key, wait for a private completion signal, then require a whole captured output line. All scopes are disposed after errors or cancellation.
examples.output: api capture ready
